# PR explainer: backlog item 254 — the stated TVL floor must derive from `DEFAULT_MIN_TVL`

**Risk tier: HIGH** (builder self-tier confirmed independently by the verifier, twice). Full walkthrough below per NORTH_STAR.md's risk policy.

## Goal

A prior, human-authorized commit (`6fceca79bb`) relaxed the product's TVL trust rail, `DEFAULT_MIN_TVL`, from $10M to $100K in `app.js`. That change itself is not in question. What broke: **nine other places that state the rail in prose never followed it** — the landing page's trust badge, the planner's Degen persona description (EN+KO, all four), `home.html`'s agent-tool contract (`navigator.modelContext`), `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt` (the AI-citation layer — north-star leg A's own surface), and a persona story page — all still said "$10M" after the real floor moved to $100K. Two generators (`generate-llms.js`, `generate-stories.js`) held their own stale, hand-typed copies of the old number, and a nightly cron (`sitemap-update.yml`) was re-publishing the false claim to `llms.txt` every 24 hours. The audit checker built to catch exactly this (`tvl-floor-claim`) never read the real constant, so it stayed green throughout.

## Intuition

The defect's mechanism is "a rail enforced once in code, re-typed by hand in N other places" — the same shape as item 212's mirror-list bug, just firing on a number instead of a list of names. The fix is not to patch nine strings (which would break identically the next time the rail moves); it's to give every stating site **one place to read the number from**, so there is nothing left to hand-retype.

## What changed, in reading order

1. **`trust-rails.js`** (new) — a small UMD module exporting `DEFAULT_MIN_TVL`, `APY_SANITY_LIMIT`, and the one `formatTvlFloor()` helper (`100000 → "$100K"`) that every consumer below now shares. `app.js` remains the sole canonical owner of the constants' *values* — this module only mirrors them for display, the same discipline `src/poller-core.js` already documents for its own independent mirror.
2. **`generate-llms.js`** — `MIN_TVL_USD`/`APY_SANITY_LIMIT`/`formatTvlFloor` now come from `require('./trust-rails.js')` instead of a second hand-typed copy. Note: `MIN_TVL_USD` was always *intended* to mirror `DEFAULT_MIN_TVL` (its own pre-existing comment said so) but had drifted stale at $10M, and it's used both for `llms.txt`'s display text *and* as the actual pool-selection floor (`isRailPassing()`). Fixing the mirror therefore changes `llms.txt`'s pool population — this was flagged and independently investigated by the verifier via `git log` archaeology: the original `6fceca79bb` commit updated every *other* sibling mirror (sitemap, snapshot generator, poller, spotlight generator) in the same commit and simply missed this one file. The fix restores parity with what the live app/sitemap already serve; it is not a new, independent decision about which pools to show.
3. **`generate-stories.js`** — same `trust-rails.js` import; kevin's `temperamentLabel` (the one persona floor claim in scope) now derives from `formatTvlFloor(TEMPERAMENTS.balanced.minTvl)` — **his own persona curation floor**, not the platform rail (see Deviations below — this was a verifier-caught bug in the first build pass). `TEMPERAMENTS` itself (the actual pool-selection floors per persona) is untouched, as the spec required.
4. **`translations.js`** — `landing.trustFloor` and `planner.personaDegenDesc` (EN + KO, four leaves total) converted from hardcoded strings to function leaves that call `TRUST_RAILS.formatTvlFloor(TRUST_RAILS.DEFAULT_MIN_TVL)`. The dictionary already supports function leaves (`createTranslationFunction` applies params), so no new mechanism was needed. KO uses the bare Latin `"$100K"` form, consistent with the KO strings the original rail-change commit already shipped elsewhere.
5. **`landing.js`** — one call site updated to invoke `copy.trustFloor` as a function (it was a plain string before).
6. **`home.html` / `plan.html`** — added a synchronous (non-`defer`) `<script src="trust-rails.js">` tag, same load-order pattern `canonical.js` already uses, so `window.TRUST_RAILS` exists before any later script reads it. `home.html`'s `navigator.modelContext` tool description (the MCP-style agent-tool contract) now derives its stated floor the same way.
7. **`audit-app.js`** — the `tvl-floor-claim` signal gained a second, **rail-relative** arm alongside its existing internal-consistency arm: it now asserts a stated floor *equals* the live `DEFAULT_MIN_TVL` (read from `app.js`, never a second hardcoded number), checked across `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and `home.html`. `stories/kevin.html` (and tomoko/lucia) are deliberately excluded — their labels state an independent persona curation floor, not a platform-rail claim.
8. **`test_rail_floor_derivation.js`** (new) — the repo-wide, test-time-enumerated scan the spec required: walks the entire parsed dictionary (all leaves, function leaves invoked) plus every served surface on disk, and asserts zero hand-typed rail figures remain. This is what the non-vacuity check (below) exercises.
9. **`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `stories/kevin.html`, `stories/tomoko.html`, `stories/lucia.html`** — regenerated via `npm run generate:llms` / `node generate-stories.js`, never hand-edited. `stories/stories.css` was also regenerated but is **byte-identical** to the pre-fix committed version (see Deviations).
10. Supporting test fixture updates (`test_llms_rails.js`, `test_llms_link_integrity.js`, `test_audit_text_surfaces.js`) — updated assertions that had themselves hardcoded the stale `$10M`/`10000000` figures (an instance of the same bug class, inside the test suite).

## Deviations from spec (both caught by the verifier, both fixed before this PR)

The first build pass shipped two defects that an independent verifier subagent caught on review, before anything was merged:

1. **`stories/kevin.html`'s label initially derived from the platform rail (`DEFAULT_MIN_TVL` → "$100K+ TVL") instead of his own persona curation floor** (`TEMPERAMENTS.balanced.minTvl`, $10M) — the exact same "stated floor ≠ actual floor" defect class this item exists to fix, just introduced fresh. Fixed by applying the same exclusion already correctly used for tomoko/lucia: kevin's label now derives from his own `TEMPERAMENTS.balanced.minTvl`, and he's excluded from the platform-rail-relative audit check on identical footing.
2. **Regenerating via `generate-stories.js` silently reverted `stories/stories.css` from the committed "Quiet" flat-design tokens (`--ui-*`) back to deprecated neumorphic tokens (`--neuro-*`)**, because a past design-reset item (225) had hand-patched the committed CSS file without updating the generator template that produces it. This predates item 254, but 254's own acceptance criteria mandated the regen, so 254 is what would have shipped the reversion. Fixed by migrating `renderStoriesCss()`'s template token-by-token; the regenerated file is now confirmed byte-identical to the pre-fix committed baseline.

Both fixes were verified independently by a second verifier pass before this PR was opened — see `product-loop-kit/specs/254-notes.md` for the full record.

## Non-vacuity (spec-required, run twice — once per verifier pass)

`DEFAULT_MIN_TVL` was temporarily bumped to `250000` in `trust-rails.js`: the repo-wide scan test and the rail-relative `tvl-floor-claim` audit signal both went RED, a regen showed `$250K` at every derived site (and correctly did *not* affect `stories/kevin.html`, which is excluded), then the value was restored to `100000` and every touched file confirmed `md5sum`-byte-identical to its pre-experiment state before re-confirming green.

## Verifier verdict

**PASS**, HIGH tier confirmed, 9/9 acceptance criteria met, on the second verification pass (first pass FAILed on the two findings above; both were fixed and independently re-verified). `DEFAULT_MIN_TVL`/`APY_SANITY_LIMIT` confirmed numerically unchanged in `app.js`. `?token=`/`?chain=`/`?pool=` sacred URLs confirmed still rendering pool cards (`test_smoke.js`, 13/13).
